problem: Navigation foundation models (VLAs) chase generality by scaling robot trajectory data and GPU-hours. Prior zero-shot LLM agents (incl. the authors' LaViRA) are single-task, drift on long instructions, and treat failed steps as discarded rather than informative.
motivation: Navigation is mostly contact-free, so its decisions (a direction in language, a pixel target in vision) lie in the natural output manifold of pretrained MLLMs and can be reasoned about by an agent rather than learned from robot data. The authors argue generality can come structurally, and that long-horizon attention drift and blind-retry recovery are the main failure modes to fix.
key_idea: Factor navigation into a training-free Language Action (direction) -> Vision Action (pixel bbox) -> Robot Action (depth back-projection + planner) pipeline, made robust by a TODO-list working memory and error-conditioned backtracking, and reuse it across four task families and four robots.
insight: Both mechanisms are needed: on R2R, removing TDM, SCB or both all give ~49-50% SR versus 60.7% for the full model, and the per-task deltas differ. TDM helps most on long-horizon and answer-driven tasks (R2R +11.4, OpenUAV +5.67), while SCB helps most on indoor object search (HM3D-v2 +9.0). A strong proprietary MLLM plus structured prompting can match trained VLAs on object search, EQA and UAV navigation, but long-instruction RxR still lags. Most failures are semantic (early stop on wrong target, 45.8% of failures) rather than geometric.
method: Unified interface: every task (VLN-CE, ObjectNav, EQA, Aerial-VLN) is cast as a language task spec + egocentric RGB-D (4-view panorama by in-place rotation; 5 cameras for the UAV) + pose + history, output as low-level actions via the factorisation A = pi_robot(phi_vis(phi_lang(.)))
Language Action Model (Gemini-3.1-Pro): every step emits one tool call from turn(dir), backtrack(wp_k), go_stair, double_check(stop) in JSON with progress_analysis and action_reasoning fields
Vision Action Model (Qwen3.5-27B): given the chosen view, returns a bounding box or point plus a target description; grounds directly on pixels with no waypoint predictor

Robot Action: back-projects the bbox pixel with depth and intrinsics to a world 3D point and plans with Fast-Marching on an accumulated 2D occupancy map (3D voxel map + visibility graph for the UAV); the only embodiment-specific part (NavDP or PX4 on real robots)

TODO List Memory (TDM): an ordered checklist of (content, status, result) sub-goals initialised from the instruction and rewritten each step via update/rewrite/add/remove ops before the action is chosen in the same MLLM call; completions without a concrete result are rolled back; prompt-only

Second Chance Backtrack (SCB): visited waypoints are stored, and backtrack triggers an FMM return to wp_k followed by a re-planning call conditioned on the failed direction and the failed trajectory images so the agent diagnoses the error and picks a new direction; the TODO list is preserved
OpenUAV adaptation: adds a downward camera and a prompt-level direction-constrained module (initial pose, current pose, goal direction, depth obstacle distance) used when grounding fails

setting.backbone: Gemini-3.1-Pro (Language Action, frozen API) + Qwen3.5-27B (Vision Action, frozen); real robots use Qwen3.5-27B-Q4 / Qwen3.5-9B-Q4 onboard
setting.model_size: Qwen3.5-27B for Vision Action (real robots: 27B-Q4 or 9B-Q4); Gemini-3.1-Pro size undisclosed
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (front camera rotated in place for 4-view panorama; UAV has 5 fixed RGB-D cameras) + pose
setting.action_space: LLM-chosen direction + pixel bbox back-projected to a 3D target; executed as discrete Habitat actions (forward 0.25 m, turn 30°, stop), AirSim 3D waypoints, or NavDP/PX4 on real robots
setting.simulator: Habitat (R2R, RxR, HM3D, MP3D-EQA) and AirSim (OpenUAV); plus real robots
setting.privileged: none beyond simulator-provided pose (and depth); the UAV uses simulator pose

numbers_note: All numbers are on stratified 100-episode subsets, not full splits. OpenUAV Easy/Hard breakdowns exist in Table 3 but are not listed separately. Real-world results are qualitative only.
results: With no training, one agent reaches 60.7 SR (R2R), 51.3 (RxR), 77.7 (HM3D-v2), 60.0 (HM3D-OVON), 54.7 ACC (MP3D-EQA) and 40.0 (OpenUAV) on 100-episode subsets. It is the best zero-shot method on all six benchmarks and beats the best trained model on HM3D-v2 (FiLM-Nav 77.0), HM3D-OVON (OmniNav 59.2), EQA (Uni-NaVid 47.3) and OpenUAV (AerialVLA 37.6). It still trails OmniNav, ABot-N0 and SPAN-Nav on R2R (69.5/66.4/66.3) and the strongest trained VLAs on RxR (e.g. NavFoM 57.4, OmniNav 73.6).
limitations: Depends on proprietary Gemini-3.1-Pro; open-weight backbones trail clearly; per-call latency is 30-150 s and cost is high (~10 EFLOPs per six-task evaluation)
Weak on long instructions (RxR) and on large-area grounding (e.g. 'hallway'); RxR SPL is only 34.0; the largest failure mode is early stop on the wrong target
Evaluation uses 100-episode subsets with high seed variance; real-world experiments are qualitative only, and dynamic obstacles/humans are handled only reactively
